instructions: Get the T-number from .TODO/config.json before adding new tasks. Assign a stable T- prefixed task number to every task in todo-next.md, todo-done.md, todo-future.md, and todo-ignore.md, and keep that number unchanged when moving the task between states. Keep todo-next.md as the only active queue. Move completed tasks to todo-done.md, deferred tasks to todo-future.md, and deliberate no-fix decisions to todo-ignore.md. Keep one task per bullet, include a Links section for related references, and store TODO metadata in .TODO/config.json. Write task descriptions as direct present-action statements and avoid retrospective phrasing such as 'now ...'. Write TODO text with super-precise language that names the current action and avoids vague reminders, hidden actors, or optional-sounding wording. Do not duplicate tasks that already exist in todo-next.md. Add generic labels from config.json to every task. Group TODO files by primary label using ## Label: label-name sections. Use (labels: label, label) on active, future, and ignore tasks. Use (labels: label, label; commit: shortsha) on done tasks, or commit: worktree until the work is committed.
suggestions: Keep TODO-next focused on important developer and end-user work.
Use shared config under data-config/frontend_shared.json and data-config/server.json for the date/alias rule source.
Document relative date calculation rules and deterministic overwriteToday behaviour.
Write task bullets as stable present-action statements, not retrospectives.
Write task bullets with super-precise wording that names the actor or owner when needed and states the exact current action.
Avoid task wording that begins with 'now', 'now also', 'now removed', 'now always', or similar changelog-style phrasing.
Write every text file as current-state behavior and current rules; mention past states, removed options, speculative possibilities, or future blockages only for risk prevention.
Update docs/AI-interaction after every durable AI instruction change, including user instructions, AI instructions, prompt examples, and post-interaction memory capture rules.
Keep reusable prompt examples in docs/AI-interaction/prompt-library as separate files and update its README.md as the index.
Use docs/AI-interaction/prompt-library/ai-memory-collection-post-interaction.md after each completed request/response cycle and keep only durable learning.
Use docs/AI-interaction/prompt-library/ai-memory-collection.md to convert it into durable project records.
Prefer compact status updates that state phase, action, result, and next action during long-running work.
Keep Railway test deploy reviews scoped to beta and dist-test unless the user explicitly names another branch.
Record broad audit findings as trace categories, then move actionable implementation into TODO-next and deferred risk prevention into TODO-future.
